answer.rationale: memory_c2 (low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply, quick onboarding, accurate invoicing) is the load-bearing record for meeting the 18% cut within 14 days; verify it before committing. memory_c6 (multi-year volume pricing) and memory_c1 (incumbent integration stability) inform the negotiation frame but do not fit the 14-day deadline or the single-decision budget. Switching primary supply to the low-cost vendor is the only candidate direction that (a) closes the full 18% mandate alone, (b) fits the 14-day expiry window, and (c) is backed by a clean prior track record of fast onboarding and accurate invoicing. Delivery-risk concern: the line runs at 94% with no buffer, so the switch must include a parallel delivery guarantee during the first cycle; if the archive contradicts the onboarding-speed claim, the fallback is negotiate_terms with the incumbent at a shorter bridge term, but that is not my current intent.
